subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` make only the isolated sandbox workspace writable while keeping the main workspace and skill instruction roots protected?
rationale: The bug is source-proven, but the repair changes the sandbox write boundary and overlaps recent security hardening, so maintainer intent is needed before automation changes the contract.

options.title: Approve isolated-writable `none`
options.body: Treat this issue as the canonical bug and update Docker, browser, fs bridge, remote bridge, SSH/OpenShell expectations, tests, and docs so `none` writes only to the per-session sandbox workspace.

options.title: Keep `none` read-only
options.body: Reject the requested behavior as the intended security posture and document which sandbox mode supports writable work.

options.title: Design a separate mode
options.body: Keep this issue open as product design for a future explicit isolated-writable mode instead of changing `none`.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated-writable `none`
recommendation.body: Treat this issue as the canonical bug and update Docker, browser, fs bridge, remote bridge, SSH/OpenShell expectations, tests, and docs so `none` writes only to the per-session sandbox workspace.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is tied to both the regression commit metadata and the adjacent sandbox security landing decision, making it the best available owner for the contract choice.
